summary: Target-level plan of Perfectoid rings and spaces, Part II: ramification and Riemann extension. RA.0 develops almost-pro-zero towers (Bhatt §3) and the amplitude-zero cone argument that carries uniform annihilation through derived tensor products. RA.1 builds the annular tower A⟨t^n/g⟩ of an integral perfectoid algebra and proves Bhatt's quantitative Riemann extension theorem with its derived form, its version without regularity and its limit form. RA.2 supplies André's uniform Banach algebra calculus: p-root and complete integral closures, the norm–unit-ball dictionary, root saturation, Laurent and Weierstrass localisations, uniform limits and colimits, root algebras and their tubular description. RA.3 constructs the perfectoid coreflection and almost perfectoid algebras and proves André's perfectoid Riemann extension theorem, the largest perfectoid subalgebra of A[1/g], and the nested-systems theorem. RA.4 proves the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma through annular envelopes, almost Galois extensions and ramified almost purity. RA.5 plans purity and almost purity, the normalized Kummer tower over W(k)⟦T_1,…,T_n⟧, André's flatness theorem (with a repaired Noetherian step), purity of Kummer extensions and ramified almost flatness modulo p^m. André's flatness lemma in Bhatt–Scholze's form is imported from PerfectoidQuotients Q3; the direct summand theorems are left to Direct summands and big Cohen–Macaulay algebras.

nodes.title: Almost-pro-zero towers and almost-pro-isomorphisms
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring, p a prime, t ∈ A and (t^{1/p^k})_{k≥0} a chosen compatible system of p-power roots (t^{1/p^0} = t, (t^{1/p^{k+1}})^p = t^{1/p^k}); write m_t for the ideal generated by all t^{1/p^k}. A tower M = (M_n)_{n≥1} of A-modules, with transition maps ρ_{n′,n}: M_{n′} → M_n for n′ ≥ n satisfying ρ_{n,n} = id and ρ_{n′,n}∘ρ_{n″,n′} = ρ_{n″,n}, is almost-pro-zero (with respect to t^{1/p^∞}) if for every k ≥ 0 and every n ≥ 1 there is n′ ≥ n such that t^{1/p^k} annihilates the image of ρ_{n′,n}. Equivalently, for every k the inclusion of towers (M_n[t^{1/p^k}])_n → (M_n)_n, where M_n[t^{1/p^k}] is the t^{1/p^k}-torsion, is an isomorphism of pro-objects. A morphism of towers of A-modules is an almost-pro-isomorphism if its kernel and cokernel towers are almost-pro-zero; a morphism of towers in D^b(A) is an almost-pro-isomorphism if for every i the tower of i-th cohomology modules of its cone is almost-pro-zero.
hypotheses: The index n′ may depend on k as well as on n. This is strictly weaker than the condition that the tower be zero as a pro-object of almost modules, where one n′ must serve every k (Bhatt Example 3.3).
No hypothesis on t is needed for the definition. The derived-limit statements of this layer assume t is a nonzerodivisor, as in Bhatt Notation 3.1.
proofSteps: If for each k the torsion subtower is pro-isomorphic to M, then for each n some transition ρ_{n′,n} factors through M_n[t^{1/p^k}], so its image is killed by t^{1/p^k}; conversely, if the image of ρ_{n′,n} is killed by t^{1/p^k}, the transition factors through the torsion submodule, which defines the inverse pro-morphism.

Almost-pro-zero towers form a Serre class among towers: subtowers and quotient towers inherit the property directly. For an extension 0 → M′ → M → M″ → 0, choose transitions into M″_n killed by t^{1/p^{k+1}} and then into M′ killed by t^{1/p^{k+1}}; the composite transition into M_n is killed by t^{2/p^{k+1}}, which divides t^{1/p^k} since p ≥ 2.
Hence almost-pro-isomorphisms of module towers satisfy two-out-of-three, and so do almost-pro-isomorphisms of towers in D^b(A), by the long exact cohomology sequences of cones.
acceptance: Bhatt Example 3.3 (computation test) and the comparison with ordinary pro-zero towers (compatibility test) pin the definition.

nodes.title: Uniformly almost-pro-zero towers relative to a second root system
nodes.statement: Let A and t be as in PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.0/almost-pro-zero-tower, and let g ∈ A carry a compatible system of p-power roots g^{1/p^k}. A tower (N_n)_{n≥1} of A-modules is uniformly almost-pro-zero with respect to g^{1/p^∞} (in t-almost modules), with constants c = (c(k))_{k≥0}, if for every k and every n ≥ 1 the image of the transition N_{n+c(k)} → N_n is annihilated by g^{1/p^k}·t^{1/p^l} for every l ≥ 0. A morphism from a constant tower f_n : L → L_n (compatible with the transitions of (L_n)) is a uniform almost-pro-isomorphism with respect to g^{1/p^∞}, with constants c, if every ker f_n is annihilated by m_t and the cokernel tower (coker f_n) is uniformly almost-pro-zero with constants c.
hypotheses: The constant c(k) must not depend on n; this uniformity is what survives derived tensor products (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.0/uniform-annihilation-derived-tensor).
Annihilation by g^{1/p^k} is measured in t-almost modules: the image must be killed by g^{1/p^k}t^{1/p^l} for all l, not by g^{1/p^k} alone.
proofSteps: A uniformly almost-pro-zero tower is almost-pro-zero with respect to the root system of tg: the image of N_{n+c(k)} → N_n is killed by g^{1/p^k}t^{1/p^k} = (tg)^{1/p^k}.
Enlarging any c(k) preserves the property, and subtowers and quotient towers inherit it with the same constants.
acceptance: The condition at k = 0 with g = 1 says the c(0)-step images are almost zero; Bhatt's Theorem 4.2 provides c(k) = p^k m.

uses.how: the cokernel tower of the annular comparison is uniformly almost-pro-zero with c(k) = p^k m
uniformity lets the estimate pass through K ⊗^L − for arbitrary complexes K with the same constants

nodes.title: Derived limits of almost-pro-zero towers are almost zero
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring with a nonzerodivisor t carrying compatible p-power roots. (1) If (M_n)_{n≥1} is an almost-pro-zero tower of A-modules, then lim_n M_n and lim¹_n M_n are almost zero, i.e. annihilated by every t^{1/p^k}; hence R lim_n M_n has almost zero cohomology. (2) If (K_n) → (L_n) is an almost-pro-isomorphism of towers in D^b(A), then R lim K_n → R lim L_n is an almost isomorphism: the cohomology of its cone is annihilated by every t^{1/p^k}.
hypotheses: Towers are indexed by n ≥ 1 (a countable cofiltered index), so R lim has amplitude [0, 1] on module towers.
For (2), the towers in D^b(A) are coherent towers in the sense of EnhancedDerivedSheaves E2, so that R lim and cones commute.
proofSteps: Fix k. The inclusion of the t^{1/p^k}-torsion subtower is a pro-isomorphism, and pro-isomorphic towers have isomorphic lim and lim¹ (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/pro-zero-derived-limit). The torsion subtower has lim and lim¹ annihilated by t^{1/p^k}, so the same holds for M.

For (2), R lim commutes with cones; the cohomology towers of the cone are almost-pro-zero by hypothesis, and the Milnor sequence (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/tower-milnor) expresses each cohomology of R lim of the cone through lim and lim¹ of these towers, which are almost zero by (1).
acceptance: For Bhatt Example 3.3 the limit is zero and lim¹ is almost zero.
If t is a unit, the statement reduces to the vanishing of lim and lim¹ of pro-zero towers.

sources.match: Shows that R lim of an almost-pro-zero pro-module has almost zero cohomology, by replacing the tower with its t^{1/p^k}-torsion subtower.
Deduces that almost-pro-isomorphisms in D^b(A) induce almost isomorphisms on R lim, by applying Lemma 3.4 to the cone.

nodes.title: Linear functors preserve almost-pro-zero towers
nodes.statement: Let A and t be as in PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.0/almost-pro-zero-tower, (M_n) an almost-pro-zero tower of A-modules and F : Mod_A → Mod_A an additive A-linear functor (F(a·φ) = a·F(φ) for a ∈ A and every A-linear map φ). Then (F(M_n))_n, with transitions F(ρ_{n′,n}), is almost-pro-zero. In particular this holds for Hom_A(N, −), Ext^i_A(N, −), N ⊗_A − and Tor_i^A(N, −) for any A-module N, and, termwise, a tower almost-pro-isomorphic to a constant tower stays so after applying such a functor.
hypotheses: F need not be exact; only A-linearity on Hom groups is used.
proofSteps: Fix k and n and choose n′ with ρ_{n′,n} factoring through M_n[t^{1/p^k}] ⊂ M_n. Then F(ρ_{n′,n}) factors through F(M_n[t^{1/p^k}]) → F(M_n).

The identity of M_n[t^{1/p^k}] multiplied by t^{1/p^k} is zero, so by A-linearity the identity of F(M_n[t^{1/p^k}]) multiplied by t^{1/p^k} is zero; hence the image of F(M_n[t^{1/p^k}]) → F(M_n) is killed by t^{1/p^k}.
acceptance: Applied to Hom_A(Q, −) for a finitely presented Q this gives the almost vanishing of lim¹ of Hom towers used in Bhatt's proof of Theorem 5.4.

sources.match: Shows that A-linear endofunctors of A-modules carry almost-pro-zero pro-modules to almost-pro-zero pro-modules, by factoring transitions through torsion submodules.

nodes.title: Uniform annihilation survives derived tensor products
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring with elements t and g carrying compatible p-power roots, and let (f_n : R → R_n)_{n≥1} be maps of R-modules into a tower (R_n) compatible with the transitions. Suppose every ker f_n is annihilated by m_t and the cokernel tower is uniformly almost-pro-zero with respect to g^{1/p^∞} with constants c(k) (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.0/uniformly-almost-pro-zero). Then for every complex K ∈ D(R) and every i ∈ Z, the kernel tower and the cokernel tower of H^i(K) → H^i(K ⊗^L_R R_n) have c(k)-step transitions annihilated by g^{1/p^k}t^{1/p^l} for every l, in particular by (tg)^{1/p^k}, for all n. The constants are independent of n, K and i.
hypotheses: The R_n need only be R-modules; in the application they are the R-algebras A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m over R = A/t^m.
The constant c(k) is the one of the cokernel tower; no constant is lost.
proofSteps: Let C_n be the cone of f_n, a complex with H^{−1}(C_n) = ker f_n and H^0(C_n) = coker f_n, and τ : C_{n+c} → C_n the transition, c = c(k).

The composite of γτ, with γ = g^{1/p^k}t^{1/p^l}, and C_n → H^0(C_n)[0] vanishes, because it factors through H^0 of the transition multiplied by γ. By the truncation triangle, γτ factors through H^{−1}(C_n)[1] → C_n.

Multiplication by t^{1/p^{l′}} kills H^{−1}(C_n), so t^{1/p^{l′}}γτ = 0 in D(R). Since m_t is idempotent, g^{1/p^k}m_t annihilates τ as a morphism of D(R) (use t^{1/p^l} = t^{1/p^{l+1}}·t^{(p−1)/p^{l+1}}).

Tensoring with K, g^{1/p^k}m_t annihilates K ⊗^L τ, hence its effect on cohomology. In the long exact sequence of K → K ⊗^L R_n → K ⊗^L C_n, the cokernel of H^i(K) → H^i(K ⊗^L R_n) embeds in H^i(K ⊗^L C_n) and the kernel is a quotient of H^{i−1}(K ⊗^L C_n), compatibly with transitions; so their c-step transitions are annihilated by g^{1/p^k}m_t.
acceptance: For K = R the statement returns the hypothesis.
For K a Koszul complex on an R-regular sequence it gives uniform almost-pro-vanishing of the higher Koszul homology of the R_n (Bhatt Remark 4.3).

sources.match: Asserts that, because the constant in Theorem 4.2 is independent of n, the kernel and cokernel pro-systems of H^i(K) → H^i(K ⊗^L A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m) are uniformly almost-pro-zero with the same constants for every complex K, and records the Koszul consequence; the cone argument written here supplies the justification Bhatt calls formal.

nodes.title: The annular tower A⟨t^n/g⟩ of an integral perfectoid algebra
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field and t ∈ K° a pseudouniformizer (0 < |t| < 1, with |t| = |p| if char K = 0) carrying compatible p-power roots. Let A be an integral perfectoid K°-algebra in Bhatt's sense: K°-flat, t-adically complete, equal to its almost elements A_* (if f ∈ A[1/t] and t^{1/p^k}f ∈ A for all k then f ∈ A), with Frobenius inducing a bijection A/t^{1/p} → A/t; let X = Spa(A[1/t], A) be its affinoid perfectoid space. Let g ∈ A carry compatible p-power roots g^{1/p^k}. For n ≥ 1 put X⟨t^n/g⟩ = {x ∈ X : |t^n(x)| ≤ |g(x)|}, a rational subset, and A⟨t^n/g⟩ = O⁺_X(X⟨t^n/g⟩). Since X⟨t^n/g⟩ ⊂ X⟨t^{n+1}/g⟩, restriction gives maps A⟨t^{n+1}/g⟩ → A⟨t^n/g⟩; with f_n : A → A⟨t^n/g⟩ they form a tower under A. In A⟨t^n/g⟩ the functions u_n^{1/p^k} := (t^n/g)^{1/p^k} are bounded, so g^{1/p^k}u_n^{1/p^k} = t^{n/p^k} and g divides t^n. For each m ≥ 0 the map A[u_n^{1/p^∞}]/(t^m, (u_n g)^{1/p^k} − t^{n/p^k} for all k) → A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m is an almost isomorphism with respect to t^{1/p^∞}, and under these presentations the transition sends u_{n+1}^e to t^e u_n^e for e ∈ Z[1/p]_{≥0}.
hypotheses: Correction PAPER-BHATT-18/E16: t must be a pseudouniformizer (0 < |t| < 1), which matters in characteristic p.
The explicit almost presentation is Scholze's Lemma 6.4, supplied by PerfectoidSpaces P2; it holds as an almost isomorphism, not on the nose.
Integral perfectoid K°-algebras and perfectoid K-algebras correspond through A ↦ A[1/t] and R ↦ R° (PerfectoidSpaces P1).
proofSteps: Rational subsets of affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid perfectoid with explicit almost integral model (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids, P2/almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization). Since g has compatible roots, the generators t^n and g of X⟨t^n/g⟩ are already of the form required there, so no approximation is needed.
The model of A⟨t^n/g⟩ is the t-adic completion of A[u^{1/p^∞}]/((ug)^{1/p^k} − t^{n/p^k})_k, up to almost isomorphism; reducing modulo t^m gives the stated presentation.
Restriction from X⟨t^{n+1}/g⟩ to X⟨t^n/g⟩ sends t^{n+1}/g to t·(t^n/g), hence u_{n+1}^e ↦ t^e u_n^e on the presentations.
acceptance: For A = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and g = T the tower is that of closed annuli |t^n| ≤ |T| ≤ 1, and A⟨t^n/T⟩ is almost K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}, (t^n/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩ (compare André A (3.12)).

nodes.title: Bhatt's quantitative Riemann extension theorem
nodes.statement: In the setting of PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.1/annular-tower, fix m ≥ 0 and assume that g is an almost nonzerodivisor modulo t^m (the kernel of multiplication by g on A/t^m is annihilated by m_t). Let f_n : A/t^m → A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m. Then, in almost mathematics with respect to t^{1/p^∞}: (1) every ker f_n is almost zero; (2) for every k ≥ 0, with c = p^k m, for every n ≥ 1 the image of the transition coker f_{n+c} → coker f_n is annihilated by g^{1/p^k}; that is, the cokernel tower is uniformly almost-pro-zero with respect to g^{1/p^∞} with constants c(k) = p^k m; (3) consequently (f_n)_n is an almost-pro-isomorphism from the constant tower A/t^m with respect to (tg)^{1/p^∞}.
hypotheses: The almost-regularity of g modulo t^m is used only for (1); PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.1/quantitative-riemann-extension-general removes it for the conclusion (3).
The constant c = p^k m depends on k and m only.
proofSteps: Replace A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m by its almost presentation M_n = A[u_n^{1/p^∞}]/(t^m, (u_ng)^{1/p^k} − t^{n/p^k}) (annular-tower).
Kernels: since g, hence each g^{1/p^k}, is an almost nonzerodivisor on A/t^m, comparing coefficients of the monomials u_n^e shows A/t^m → M_n is almost injective.

Cokernels: the c-fold transition sends g^{1/p^k}u_{n+c}^e to g^{1/p^k}t^{ce}u_n^e. If e ≥ 1/p^k then ce ≥ m and the term is zero modulo t^m. If e < 1/p^k it equals g^{1/p^k−e}t^{ce}(gu_n)^e = g^{1/p^k−e}t^{(n+c)e}, which lies in the image of A/t^m. So g^{1/p^k} kills the image of coker f_{n+c} → coker f_n.
(3) follows from (1), (2) and PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.0/uniformly-almost-pro-zero.
acceptance: The constant c = p^k m works for every n.
For m = 0 all rings are zero and the statement is empty.
For A = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and g = T, (3) is the integral almost form of the statement that bounded functions on the punctured perfectoid disc extend.
The non-example of PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.1/annular-tower shows (1) fails without the hypothesis on g.

nodes.title: Derived form of the quantitative Riemann extension theorem
nodes.statement: In the setting of PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.1/quantitative-riemann-extension (g almost regular modulo t^m, m ≥ 1), for every complex K ∈ D(A/t^m) and every i ∈ Z the kernel and cokernel towers of H^i(K) → H^i(K ⊗^L_{A/t^m} A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m) have p^k m-step transitions annihilated by g^{1/p^k} in t-almost modules, hence by (tg)^{1/p^k} in modules, for every k and n; the constants do not depend on n, K or i. In particular, if x_1, …, x_r is a regular sequence in A/t^m, then for j ≠ 0 the Koszul homology towers H_j(Kos(A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m; x)) are uniformly almost-pro-zero with respect to g^{1/p^∞} (in t-almost modules).

proofSteps: Apply PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.0/uniform-annihilation-derived-tensor with R = A/t^m, R_n = A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m and the constants c(k) = p^k m from Theorem 4.2.

For the Koszul statement take K = Kos(A/t^m; x) (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1/koszul-complex), quasi-isomorphic to (A/t^m)/(x) by regularity; K ⊗^L R_n = Kos(R_n; x) and H^i(K) = 0 for i ≠ 0, so the comparison towers in nonzero degrees are the Koszul homology towers themselves.
acceptance: For K = A/t^m this is Theorem 4.2.
The Koszul consequence is the case Bhatt records in Remark 4.3.

nodes.title: Quantitative Riemann extension without regularity of g
nodes.statement: Let A be an integral perfectoid K°-algebra and g ∈ A with compatible p-power roots, with no regularity hypothesis on g. For every m ≥ 0 the map of towers (A/t^m)_n → (A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m)_n is an almost-pro-isomorphism with respect to (tg)^{1/p^∞}.
hypotheses: Only the conclusion (3) of Theorem 4.2 survives; almost injectivity of each f_n can fail (see the non-example of PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.1/annular-tower).
proofSteps: Universal case: R = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ with g = T. Here R/t^m = (K°/t^m)[T^{1/p^∞}], on which T is a nonzerodivisor, so Theorem 4.2 applies: (R/t^m) → (R⟨t^n/T⟩/t^m) is an almost-pro-isomorphism with respect to (tT)^{1/p^∞}.

There is a unique continuous K°-algebra map R → A sending T^{1/p^k} to g^{1/p^k} (the universal property of the perfected Tate algebra, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfected-tate-algebra, at the integral level). Base change along R/t^m → A/t^m preserves almost-pro-isomorphisms by the derived form (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.1/quantitative-riemann-extension-derived with K = A/t^m regarded over R/t^m).
The almost presentations of annular-tower are compatible with base change, so R⟨t^n/T⟩ ⊗_R A/t^m is almost A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m; taking H^0 gives the claim.
acceptance: For g a nonzerodivisor modulo t^m this recovers Theorem 4.2(3).
For g = 0 the root ideal of tg is zero, every module is almost zero for it, and the statement is empty; this matches A⟨t^n/0⟩ = 0.

nodes.statement: Let A be an integral perfectoid K°-algebra and g ∈ A with compatible p-power roots. Take R lim over m: A and each A⟨t^n/g⟩ are t-adically complete and the towers over m have surjective transitions, so lim over m and over n commute and no lim¹ in m appears; the almost isomorphism passes to the limit by PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits.

nodes.title: p-root closure and the localised complete integral closure
nodes.statement: Let R → S be an injective map of commutative rings and p a prime. An element s ∈ S is p-radicial over R if s^{p^n} ∈ R for some n ≥ 0, and R is p-root closed in S if s ∈ S and s^p ∈ R imply s ∈ R. The p-root closure R^†_S is the smallest subring of S that contains R and is p-root closed in S; it is the increasing union of R_0 = R and R_{i+1} = the subring generated by the elements p-radicial over R_i. When R has characteristic p, or S = R[1/p], the p-radicial elements already form a subring, equal to R^†_S. For g ∈ R a nonzerodivisor of S with S = R[1/g], the localised complete integral closure is R^*_S = {s ∈ S : there is m with g^m s^n ∈ R for all n ≥ 0}; it is the set of s whose powers lie in a finitely generated R-submodule of S. One has R ⊂ R^†_S ⊂ R^+_S ⊂ R^*_S, where R^+_S is the integral closure.
hypotheses: André's complete integral closure is defined by finitely generated submodules of S; Mathlib's completeIntegralClosure uses a multiplier from the nonzerodivisors of R. For S = R[1/g] with g ∈ R⁰, André's is contained in Mathlib's (take the multiplier g^m); for a Noetherian domain and its fraction field both equal the integral closure.
proofSteps: The union of the R_i is p-root closed (if s^p ∈ R_i then s ∈ R_{i+1}), and any p-root closed intermediate ring contains every R_i by induction; so the union is the minimum.
In characteristic p, (a + b)^{p^n} = a^{p^n} + b^{p^n} and (ab)^{p^n} = a^{p^n}b^{p^n}, so p-radicial elements form a subring; for S = R[1/p] André cites Roberts for the same conclusion.
A p-radicial element is integral, and an integral element of R[1/g] has its powers in the finitely generated module spanned by its first d powers, so R^† ⊂ R^+ ⊂ R^*.
A finitely generated R-submodule of R[1/g] lies in g^{-m}R for some m, which gives the description of R^*_S.
acceptance: The chain R^†_S ⊂ R^+_S can be strict, and the description of R^*_S in R[1/g] is the formula André uses in (2.18)–(2.19).

nodes.title: The norm–unit-ball dictionary for uniform Banach algebras
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value, ϖ ∈ K°° nonzero and Γ ⊂ R with |ϖ|^Γ = |K^×|. (a) For a K°-flat K°-algebra A, the gauge |a| = |ϖ|^r with r = sup{s ∈ Γ : ϖ^{-s}a ∈ A} is a seminorm on A[1/ϖ], a norm iff A has no nonzero infinitely ϖ-divisible element; its unit ball is A when Γ is discrete and A_* = ⋂_{s ∈ Γ_{>0}} ϖ^{-s}A otherwise; a ring map φ : A[1/ϖ] → A′[1/ϖ] with φ(A) ⊂ A′ is continuous, and φ^{-1}(A′) = A is sufficient for it to be isometric. The exact criterion is φ^{-1}(A′_{≤1}) = A_{≤1} for the actual gauge unit balls (equal to A_* and A′_* in the nondiscrete case). (b) If |K| is dense in the norm values of a normed K-algebra A with unit ball A_{≤1}, then A^†_A ⊂ A^+_A ⊂ A^*_A = A° for the closures of A_{≤1}, and (A^†_A)_* is the unit ball of the spectral seminorm. (c) Under (b) the following are equivalent: the norm is spectral (power-multiplicative); A_{≤1} = A°; A_{≤1} is completely integrally closed in A; it is integrally closed in A; it is p-root closed in A; and, when |ϖ| ≥ |p| and 1/p ∈ Γ, Frobenius A_{≤1}/ϖ^{1/p} → A_{≤1}/ϖ is injective. (d) If |K| is dense in R_{>0}, B ↦ B° is an equivalence from uniform Banach K-algebras with continuous homomorphisms to K°-algebras B that are K°-flat, ϖ-adically complete, completely integrally closed (equivalently integrally closed, or p-root closed) in B[1/ϖ], and equal to Hom_{K°}(K°°, B); a quasi-inverse is B ↦ (B[1/ϖ], gauge norm). The same holds relative to a fixed uniform Banach K-algebra.
hypotheses: Uniform means that A° is bounded, equivalently that the norm is equivalent to the spectral seminorm (with the corrected constant of PAPER-ANDRE-18/E20).
Density of |K| in R_{>0} holds when the valuation of K is not discrete, for instance for perfectoid K.
proofSteps: Construct the gauge using flatness. A linear map is an isometry exactly when it preserves and reflects every norm bound, equivalently the actual gauge unit ball and its scalar dilates. Equality φ^{-1}(A′) = A implies this after taking the intersections defining A_*; the converse for arbitrary lattices is not asserted.

(b) An element is power-bounded iff its powers lie in a finitely generated A_{≤1}-submodule, so A^*_A = A°. The gauge of the p-root closure is lim |a^{p^n}|^{1/p^n}, the spectral seminorm, by Fekete's lemma.
(c) combines (a), (b) and the inclusion of closures; Frobenius injectivity modulo ϖ is p-root closedness read on reductions.
(d) The four conditions characterise unit balls of spectral norms by (a) and (c); continuous maps of uniform algebras preserve power-bounded elements.
acceptance: André's example K°[ϖT, …, ϖ^{i+1}T^{p^i}, …] ⊂ K°[T] (Remarque 2.3.3(2)) shows A^+ ⊂ A^* = A° ⊂ spectral unit ball can all be strict, and that a complete integral closure need not be completely integrally closed.

For densely valued K, take A = K° + K°°T K°[T] ⊂ A′ = K°[T]. Both generic fibres are K[T] and both gauge norms are Gauss, since scalar factors of norm just above 1 clear each of the finitely many coefficients. Thus the identity is isometric although T ∈ A′ ∖ A. This distinguishes a gauge unit ball from the original lattice.

nodes.title: The root saturation g^{-1/p^∞}B° and its closedness
nodes.statement: Let K have |K| dense in R_{>0} and let B be a uniform Banach K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra, with g^{1/p^m} the image of T^{1/p^m}; equivalently a uniform Banach K-algebra with a compatible system of p-power roots of g ∈ B°. The root saturation is g^{-1/p^∞}B° = ⋂_m g^{-1/p^m}B° = {b ∈ B°[1/g] : g^{1/p^m}b ∈ B° for all m}. In the almost setup (V, m) = (K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, T^{1/p^∞}K°°V) it is the module of almost elements: (B°ᵃ)_* = lim along multiplication by g^{1/p^m − 1/p^{m+1}} of B°, which maps injectively to B°[1/g] with image g^{-1/p^∞}B°; this image is ϖ-adically complete, and B° → g^{-1/p^∞}B° is injective iff g is a nonzerodivisor of B. The following are equivalent (André A Lemme 2.5.3): g^{-1/p^∞}B° is p-root closed in B°[1/g]; it is p-root closed in B[1/g]; it equals the complete integral closure of B° in B°[1/g]; it equals the complete integral closure of B° in B[1/g]; it is completely integrally closed in B°[1/g]; it is completely integrally closed in B[1/g]. Root saturation commutes with projective limits of such algebras: g^{-1/p^∞}(lim B_α°) = lim g^{-1/p^∞}B_α°.
hypotheses: The formula (2.17) of André A has a misprint: the middle term is g^{-1/p^∞}B°[1/ϖ], not [1/p] (PAPER-ANDRE-18/E5).
In the proof of (2) ⇒ (6) the condition invoked is (2), not (1) (PAPER-ANDRE-18/E11).
proofSteps: Since B is uniform, Hom_V(V°°, B°) = B°; as m is the colimit of V°° along multiplication by T^{1/p^m − 1/p^{m+1}}, (B°ᵃ)_* is the stated limit, a reduced ring on which g is almost a nonzerodivisor; hence it embeds in B°[1/g] with image g^{-1/p^∞}B°. Completeness follows from Lemme 2.3.4 (almost elements preserve completeness).

For the closedness conditions, g^{-1/p^∞}B° ⊂ B°^*_{B°[1/g]} ⊂ B°^*_{B[1/g]} ⊂ (g^{-1/p^∞}B°)^*_{B[1/g]}, so the last condition implies the others; (1) ⇒ (2) uses the spectral unit-ball dictionary, and (2) ⇒ (6) uses that ϖ^{m/p^n}g^{m/p^n}b lies in g^{-1/p^∞}B° for all n.
Compatibility with limits: almostification and almost elements preserve limits, or exchange the limits over m and α.
acceptance: If g is invertible in B then g^{-1/p^∞}B° = B° (André A Lemme 2.5.2).
For a ring R with compatible roots of a nonzerodivisor t, R^*_{R[1/t]} = t^{-1/p^∞}R^†_{R[1/t]} (André A Remarque 2.5.6), a purely algebraic form suitable for the suggested Lean file.

nodes.title: Laurent localisation A{λ/g} of a uniform Banach algebra
nodes.statement: Let K be complete nonarchimedean and A a uniform Banach K-algebra. For f_1, …, f_n, f ∈ A generating the unit ideal, A{f_1,…,f_n/f} = A⟨U_1,…,U_n⟩/(fU_i − f_i)^−, the quotient by the closure of the ideal; it is the universal Banach A-algebra in which f is invertible and the f_i/f are power-bounded. For 0 ≠ λ ∈ K° and g = λf ∈ A°, A{λ/g} := A{1/f} = A⟨U⟩/(fU − 1)^−, regarded as a K⟨T⟩-algebra through T ↦ g. Properties: the ideal (fU − 1) is closed when A is uniform, so the closure is unnecessary; A{λ/g} ≅ A ⊗̂_{K⟨T⟩} K⟨T⟩{λ/T} isometrically; A{λ/g} = 0 when g ∈ λA°°; for |λ| ≤ |μ| there are canonical maps A{λ/g} → A{μ/g} and A{μ/g} ≅ A{λ/g}{μ/g}; if |g − h| < |λ| then A{λ/g} ≅ A{λ/h}; the image of a ∈ A has quotient norm inf_{h ∈ A⟨U⟩} ‖a + (fU − 1)h‖_Gauss, not in general inf_m |(g/λ)^m a|. The uniformization A{λ/g}^u (AdicSpacesPartII R0) is the left adjoint, on uniform K⟨T⟩-algebras, of the inclusion of those in which T/λ is invertible with power-bounded inverse. Gabber's invariance: if g is a nonzerodivisor and A ⊂ A′ ⊂ A[1/g] is a Banach algebra extension, then A{λ/g} → A′{λ/g} is an isomorphism. If moreover A is uniform, A° → lim_{λ→0} A{λ/g}° is injective.
hypotheses: The lower-bound slip in Lemme 2.6.3 and the stronger false norm formula on pp. 28–29 are separate issues (E3 and E11). The limit-injectivity conclusion is retained using a spectral-point argument. Restriction maps between individual annuli need not be injective (E4).
A{λ/g} need not be uniform; only its uniformization is used in the uniform category.
proofSteps: A{λ/g} is the rational localisation of the Huber pair (A, A°) at {λ, g}/g (AdicSpaces Layer 3 and AdicSpacesPartII R0), so its universal property is the one of rational localisation.

For closedness (André A Lemme 2.6.1, after Mihara), replace the uniform norm by the equivalent spectral norm. At each bounded multiplicative point x, extend to the Gauss seminorm on A⟨U⟩: ‖(fU−1)h‖_x = max(1,|f(x)|)‖h‖_x ≥ ‖h‖_x. Taking the supremum over x gives the spectral Gauss norm and bounds multiplication by fU−1 below. Its image is therefore complete and closed. The same closedness holds for the original equivalent norm.

The completed-tensor presentation and transition maps follow from their presentations and universal properties. If ‖g−h‖ < |λ|, use the convergent expansion 1/h = Σ_{m≥0}(g−h)^m/g^{m+1} inside A{λ/g}; the difference 1/h−1/g starts at m = 1. The norm is the quotient norm, obtained by varying all h ∈ A⟨U⟩.
Gabber's invariance: by Baire and the open mapping theorem, multiplication by a power g^N maps A′ continuously into A, which gives a continuous inverse after inverting g in A{λ/g}.

For nonzero a and a nonzerodivisor g, ag ≠ 0. The spectral seminorm of a uniform Banach algebra is a norm, so choose a bounded multiplicative seminorm x with |a(x)g(x)| > 0 (AdicSpacesPartII R3). Choose nonzero λ ∈ K° with |λ| ≤ |g(x)|. This point extends to A{λ/g}, where it detects the image of a. Hence A → lim_{λ→0} A{λ/g}, and therefore A° → lim A{λ/g}°, is injective. No lower bound uniform in all points is needed.
acceptance: For A = K⟨T⟩, g = T and 0 < |λ| ≤ 1, A{λ/T} = K⟨T, λ/T⟩ is the closed annulus |λ| ≤ |T| ≤ 1. Its quotient norm is spectral and is multiplicative exactly when |λ| = 1.

nodes.title: Weierstrass localisation B{f/λ} and its unit ball
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a nontrivial valuation, 0 ≠ λ ∈ K°, B a uniform Banach K-algebra and f ∈ B_{≤1}. Then B{f/λ} = B⟨U⟩/(λU − f), the ideal being closed; if f is a nonzerodivisor of B then so is λU − f in B⟨U⟩. Suppose |K| is dense in |B| and multiplication by f is isometric (e.g. the norm is multiplicative and |f| = 1). Then B_{≤1}⟨U⟩/(λU − f) is torsion-free over K°, (λU − f)B_{≤1}⟨U⟩ = ((λU − f)B⟨U⟩)_{≤1}, and B{f/λ}_{≤1} = B_{≤1}⟨U⟩/(λU − f) if the valuation is discrete, B{f/λ}_{≤1} = (B_{≤1}⟨U⟩/(λU − f))_* otherwise. Moreover (λU − f)B_{≤1}⟨U⟩ is closed, B_{≤1}⟨U⟩/(λU − f) is ϖ-adically separated and equals the ϖ-adic completion of B_{≤1}[f/λ] ⊂ B, through the exact sequence 0 → (λU − f)B_{≤1}[U] → B_{≤1}[U] → B_{≤1}[f/λ] → 0 and its completion. Finally B_{≤1}⟨U⟩/(λU − f) does not change, up to isomorphism, when f is replaced by f′ with |f − f′| ≤ |λ| or λ by λ′ with |λ′| = |λ|; the map from the new presentation to the old one sends U_new ↦ (λ/λ′)U_old + (f′−f)/λ′.
hypotheses: André's argument for torsion-freeness is written for λ-torsion; the same computation with an arbitrary nonzero μ ∈ K° gives torsion-freeness over K°, which is what is used (the extraction's E14 records this reading; its review rejected it as an error).
The conditional in formula (2) of André B reads 'if the valuation of K is discrete' (misprint PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/E15).
proofSteps: Closedness of the ideal is the Weierstrass case of André A Lemme 2.6.1 (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.2/laurent-localisation).

If μ·Σ b_m U^m = (λU − f)Σ a_m U^m with a_m ∈ B_{≤1}, comparing coefficients and using that multiplication by f is injective modulo μ (it is isometric) shows μ divides every a_m; this gives torsion-freeness and the equality of unit balls, then (2)/(3) by the gauge dictionary (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.2/unit-ball-dictionary).
The polynomial sequence is exact by the same torsion-freeness; its completion is right exact with dense image of (λU − f)B_{≤1}⟨U⟩ in the kernel, and closedness gives exactness, whence (4).

The substitution U_new ↦ (λ/λ′)U_old + (f′−f)/λ′ is bounded on integral Tate algebras and sends λ′U_new−f′ to λU_old−f. Its inverse is U_old ↦ (λ′/λ)U_new+(f−f′)/λ; this proves invariance in the indicated direction.
acceptance: For B = K⟨T⟩ (Gauss norm), f = T and λ = ϖ, B{T/ϖ} = K⟨T/ϖ⟩ is the disc of radius |ϖ| and its unit ball is K°⟨U⟩ with T = ϖU.
The invariance under |f − f′| ≤ |λ| is what allows André B to replace (T − g)^{1/p^k} by an element of a Noetherian stage (formula (14)).

nodes.title: Uniform limits of uniform Banach algebras
nodes.statement: Let K be complete nonarchimedean. The category K-uBan of uniform Banach K-algebras with continuous homomorphisms has all small limits. For a projective system (A_α) indexed by a (not necessarily filtered) ordered set, the uniform limit is ulim A_α = {a = (a_α) ∈ lim A_α : sup_α |a_α|_sp < ∞} with the norm sup_α |a_α|_sp; it is a spectral Banach K-algebra and (ulim A_α)° = lim A_α°. Consequently the four conditions of the unit-ball dictionary are preserved by limits. The map (ulim A_α)°/ϖ → lim(A_α°/ϖ) is injective.
hypotheses: The uniform limit is computed with spectral norms; it differs in general from the limit in perfectoid algebras (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/uniform-limit-perfectoid-criterion).
|K| dense in R_{>0} is needed for the unit-ball statements.
proofSteps: Equalizers are closed subalgebras and products exist (bounded families in spectral norm), so the category is complete; the explicit formula is the limit of sets cut down by boundedness.
The unit ball for the sup of spectral norms is the set of families with every a_α power-bounded, i.e. lim A_α°.
Injectivity modulo ϖ: each A_α° is ϖ-torsion-free, so 0 → lim A_α° —ϖ→ lim A_α° → lim(A_α°/ϖ) is exact.
acceptance: The closed discs of radii r_i ↑ 1 have uniform limit K°⟦T⟧ ⊗ K, the bounded functions on the open unit disc.
The annuli K⟨T, ϖ^j/T⟩ have uniform limit K⟨T⟩, the simplest nonarchimedean Riemann extension.

nodes.title: Uniform filtered colimits of uniform Banach algebras
nodes.statement: Let (B_α) be a filtered inductive system of uniform Banach K-algebras. The colimit seminorm |(b_α)| = lim_α |b_α|_sp on colim B_α is well defined, and the uniform colimit ucolim B_α is the separated completion of colim B_α for it, a spectral Banach K-algebra; equivalently, the uniformization (AdicSpacesPartII R0) of the colimit Tate ring. It is the filtered colimit in K-uBan, and (ucolim B_α)° = (completed colim B_α°)_*; if the norms are spectral and the transitions isometric, the maps B_β → ucolim B_α are isometric and (ucolim B_α)° is the completed colimit of the unit balls. K-uBan is cocomplete, with pushouts the uniform completed tensor products, and uniform colimits commute with the uniform localisations (·){λ/g}^u.
hypotheses: The colimit in K-uBan is not the colimit of underlying rings: separation and completion for the spectral seminorm intervene (André A Exemple 2.9.3(4)).
proofSteps: Monotonicity of spectral seminorms along continuous maps makes the limit seminorm well defined and power-multiplicative; its separated completion receives compatible maps and has the universal property among uniform algebras.
The unit-ball formula follows from the gauge dictionary (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.2/unit-ball-dictionary).

Cocompleteness: filtered colimits, pushouts ⊗̂^u and an initial object K give all colimits. Commutation with localisation: ucolim commutes with ⊗̂^u, and A{λ/g}^u ≅ A ⊗̂^u_{K⟨T⟩} K⟨T⟩{λ/T} (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.2/laurent-localisation).
acceptance: In characteristic p, the completed perfection of K is ucolim K^{1/p^i}.
Every uniform Banach K-algebra is a filtered uniform colimit of reduced affinoid algebras with bijective algebraic colimit map (André A Exemple 2.9.3(3)).

nodes.title: The perfectoid coreflection A ↦ A^♮
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field. For a uniform Banach K-algebra A, A♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} A is a perfectoid K♭-algebra (PerfectoidSpaces P1, tilt of a uniform Tate ring), and A^♮ := (A♭)^♯ is the perfectoid K-algebra corresponding to it under the tilting equivalence. There is a canonical map A^♮ → A; with spectral norms it is isometric, and it is an isomorphism iff A is perfectoid. The functor ♮ is right adjoint to the inclusion of perfectoid K-algebras into uniform Banach K-algebras, so perfectoid K-algebras form a coreflective full subcategory, and ♭ is right adjoint to ι∘♯. In characteristic p, A^♮ = ulim_F A. Limits of perfectoid algebras exist and are computed as (ulim)^♮.
hypotheses: The counit A^♮ → A need not be surjective, and A^♮°/ϖ → A°/ϖ is injective.

In characteristic p, Frobenius is semilinear over K, not generally K-linear. The tower ulim_F is formed on underlying normed rings with the successive K-actions twisted by Frobenius; it then has the compatible K-algebra structure required by the coreflection.
proofSteps: A^♮°/ϖ ≅ A♭°/ϖ♭ → A°/ϖ is injective (André A Proposition 3.3.1), which gives the isometry of the counit; ♮ restricted to perfectoid algebras is the identity, which gives the adjunction.
♭ restricted to perfectoid algebras has ♯ as quasi-inverse, so ♭ = ♭|∘♮ is right adjoint to ι∘♯ by composing adjunctions.
acceptance: For A perfectoid, A^♮ = A.
For A = K⟨T⟩ (not perfectoid), A^♮ = K: the tilt of K⟨T⟩ is K♭, as T has no compatible p-power roots.

nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field and A a perfectoid K-algebra. (2) If A is spectral and g ∈ A°, then A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid; the canonical map A ⊗̂_K K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩ is an extremal epimorphism of uniform Banach algebras, and the compatible roots of g define g♭ ∈ A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩♭ with (g♭)^♯ = g.
hypotheses: (2) uses that extremal quotients of perfectoid algebras are perfectoid, because perfectoid algebras form a coreflective subcategory whose counits are monomorphisms (André A §3.6.1).
proofSteps: (1): A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = A ⊗̂_K K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is a completed tensor product of perfectoid algebras, hence perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid, P1/perfected-tate-algebra); the universal property is the root-algebra universal property.

(2): A ⊗̂ K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → A⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩ is an extremal epimorphism by the quotient description (2.30); coreflectivity (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/perfectoid-coreflection) shows extremal quotients of perfectoid algebras are perfectoid. The element g♭ is the inverse system of the g^{1/p^k} modulo p.

nodes.statement: Let K be perfectoid and work in the almost setup (V, m) = (K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, T^{1/p^∞}K°°V). A uniform Banach K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra B is almost perfectoid if Bˆᵃ is isomorphic in this category to a perfectoid K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra. Equivalent conditions: B is almost perfectoid; Frobenius is almost surjective on B°/ϖ; B^♮° → B° is an almost isomorphism; B^♮ → B is an almost isomorphism; some perfectoid B′ maps to B by a map that is an almost isomorphism; (Bˆᵃ)ˆ!! is perfectoid. (2) ⇒ (3): by Nakayama it suffices that lim_F(B°/ϖ) → B°/ϖ is almost surjective, which follows from almost surjectivity of Frobenius by Mittag-Leffler for F_p-vector spaces; (5) ⇒ (1) by André A Lemme 2.3.5; (3) ⇒ (6) by adjunction.

nodes.title: Annular localisations of perfectoid algebras and their integral models
nodes.statement: Let K be perfectoid with ϖ = (ϖ♭)^♯ and roots ϖ^{1/p^i} = ((ϖ♭)^{1/p^i})^♯. For the standard algebra, K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{ϖ^j/T}° = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}, (ϖ^j/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩, the completion of K°[T^{1/p^∞}, U^{1/p^∞}]/(T^{1/p^k}U^{1/p^k} − ϖ^{j/p^k})_k, while its unit ball for the quotient norm is K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}, ϖ^j/T⟩. For A a perfectoid K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra with spectral norm and g = T·1, every A{ϖ^j/g} is perfectoid, A{ϖ^j/g} ≅ A ⊗̂_{K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩} K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{ϖ^j/T}, and the canonical map (A° ⊗̂_{K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩} K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}, (ϖ^j/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩)_* → A{ϖ^j/g}° is an isomorphism; if char K = 0, A{ϖ^j/g}♭ = A♭{(ϖ♭)^j/g♭}.

nodes.title: Scholze's limit lemma for root localisations
nodes.statement: Let K be perfectoid of residue characteristic p, ϖ ∈ K°° with pK° ⊂ ϖK° and roots ϖ^{1/p^i} as above, r ∈ N[1/p], and R a (K°/ϖ^r)[T^{1/p^∞}]-algebra. Put R[j] = R ⊗_{K°[T^{1/p^∞}]} K°[T^{1/p^∞}, (ϖ^j/T)^{1/p^∞}] for j ∈ N, with transition maps sending u^s_{[j+1]} = 1 ⊗ (ϖ^{j+1}/T)^s to ϖ^s u^s_{[j]}; note T^s u^s_{[j]} = ϖ^{js}. Then the canonical map R → lim_j R[j] is an almost isomorphism in the setup (K°[T^{1/p^∞}], (ϖT)^{1/p^∞}K°[T^{1/p^∞}]).

proofSteps: Introduce the submodules R[j]_k = Σ_{s ∈ N[1/p] ∩ [0, 1/p^k]} R·u^s_{[j]}. Since u^s_{[j′]} maps to 0 in R[j] when s(j′ − j) ≥ r, the transition R[j′] → R[j] factors through R[j]_k for j′ ≥ j + rp^k; hence lim_j R[j] = lim_{j,k} R[j]_k.
T^{1/p^k} maps R[j]_k into the image S_j of R, so (S_j)ᵃ = lim_k (R[j]_k)ᵃ.
The kernel of R → S_j is killed by T^{r/j} for j = p^ℓ, by comparing coefficients of a presentation. Combining gives Rᵃ = lim_j (S_j)ᵃ = lim_j R[j]ᵃ.

nodes.title: André's perfectoid Riemann extension theorem
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of residue characteristic p, A a perfectoid (or almost perfectoid) K-algebra, and g ∈ A° a nonzerodivisor admitting a compatible system of p-power roots in A. Then lim_j A{ϖ^j/g}° = g^{-1/p^∞}A°, and this ring is the complete integral closure of A° in A[1/g]. Moreover, for every perfectoid K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra B with g the image of T, g^{-1/p^∞}B° is completely integrally closed in B[1/g] (André A Lemme 4.2.3). If multiplication by g is isometric, ulim_j A{ϖ^j/g} = g^{-1/p^∞}A, the complete integral closure of A in A[1/g].
hypotheses: The roots of g are part of the hypothesis; without them, André only shows the limit is contained in the complete integral closure, under an Ax–Sen–Tate type invariance (Remarque 4.2.5).
proofSteps: Reduce the almost perfectoid case to the perfectoid case by replacing A with A^♮, which still contains the roots of g.

By PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/annular-localisation-perfectoid, A°⟨(ϖ^j/g)^{1/p^∞}⟩ → A{ϖ^j/g}° is an almost isomorphism; apply PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/scholze-limit-lemma to R = A°/ϖ^r to get (A°/ϖ^r)ᵃ = lim_j (A{ϖ^j/g}°/ϖ^r)ᵃ, then let r → ∞ and interchange limits: (A°)ᵃ = lim_j (A{ϖ^j/g}°)ᵃ.
Apply almost elements, which commute with limits, and the root-saturation formula (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.2/root-saturation): g^{-1/p^∞}A° = lim_j A{ϖ^j/g}°.

Lemme 4.2.3: if a ∈ B°[1/g] and a^p ∈ g^{-1/p^∞}B°, then in each B{ϖ^j/g}^u a power-bounded multiple of a has power-bounded p-th power, so a is power-bounded there (spectral unit balls are p-root closed); passing to the limit a ∈ g^{-1/p^∞}B°. Hence condition (1) of André A Lemme 2.5.3 holds, and the root saturation is the complete integral closure.
acceptance: For A = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and g = T: lim_j K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{ϖ^j/T}° = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, bounded functions on the punctured perfectoid disc extend.
For André's Â_∞ (Exemple 4.2.6) the theorem combined with Wintenberger's Ax–Sen–Tate theorem gives Â°_∞ = lim Â_∞{p^j/g}°.

(1) (g^{-1/p^∞}A°[1/ϖ])^♮ is the largest spectral perfectoid A-algebra contained in A[1/g] (with continuous structure map from A). hypotheses: 'Contained in A[1/g]' is as abstract A-algebras; the topology is the one making the structure map continuous.
proofSteps: (1) For A ⊂ A′ ⊂ A[1/g] perfectoid spectral, Gabber's invariance (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.2/laurent-localisation) identifies A{ϖ^j/g} and A′{ϖ^j/g}; the Riemann extension theorem for A and A′ gives g^{-1/p^∞}A°[1/ϖ] = g^{-1/p^∞}A′°[1/ϖ], which contains A′ = A′^♮; apply the coreflection.
(2) Tilt the limit formula using PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/annular-localisation-perfectoid: (lim A{ϖ^j/g}°)♭ = lim A♭{(ϖ♭)^j/g♭}°.
acceptance: For A = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and g = T, g^{-1/p^∞}A° = A°, so A itself is the largest perfectoid A-algebra inside A[1/T]: bounded functions on the punctured perfectoid disc are already functions on the disc.

nodes.title: When is a uniform limit of perfectoid algebras perfectoid
nodes.statement: Let K be perfectoid of characteristic 0, ϖ with pK° ⊂ ϖK° and ϖ_{1/p} of norm |ϖ|^{1/p}. For a projective system (A_α) of perfectoid K-algebras with uniform limit A (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.2/uniform-limit) and perfectoid limit A^♮, consider: (1) A is perfectoid; (2) A^♮ → A is an isomorphism; (3) A^♮°/ϖ → lim(A_α°/ϖ) is almost surjective; (4) the Frobenius-induced map lim(A_α°/ϖ) ⊗_{K°/ϖ, F} K°/ϖ → lim(A_α°/ϖ) is almost surjective; (5) lim(A_α°/ϖ) → lim(A_α°/ϖ_{1/p}) is almost surjective. Then (1) ⇔ (2) ⇐ (3) ⇔ (4) ⇔ (5). The same argument in the setup (K°[T^{1/p^∞}], T^{1/p^∞}K°°K°[T^{1/p^∞}]) shows: if (A_α) are perfectoid K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebras and lim(A_α°/ϖ) → lim(A_α°/ϖ_{1/p}) is almost surjective, then A is almost perfectoid and A°/ϖ → lim(A_α°/ϖ) is an almost isomorphism.
hypotheses: A uniform limit of perfectoid algebras need not be perfectoid (André A Exemple prophylactique 3.8.5).
proofSteps: (A^♮)♭° = A♭° = lim_F L with L = lim(A_α°/ϖ) (formula (3.17)).
(4) ⇔ (5): the Frobenius map factors through L/ϖ_{1/p} → L_{1/p} and the compatible Frobenius isomorphisms of the A_α.
(4) ⇒ (3): almost surjectivity of Frobenius gives surjectivity of F on K°°L, hence, by Mittag-Leffler for F_p-vector spaces, almost surjectivity of lim_F L → L.
(3) + (4) ⇒ (1): A°/ϖ → L is injective (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.2/uniform-limit), hence an almost isomorphism, and Frobenius on A°/ϖ is almost surjective; (1) ⇔ (2) by the coreflection.
acceptance: For a constant system all conditions hold.

sources.match: Compares the uniform and perfectoid limits of a projective system of perfectoid algebras through conditions on the limit of reductions modulo ϖ.
Transfers the argument to the ramified setup and concludes almost perfectoidness of the uniform limit.

nodes.title: Vanishing of lim¹ for nested root-localisation systems
nodes.statement: In the setting of PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/scholze-limit-lemma, work in (K°[T^{1/p^∞}], (ϖT)^{1/p^∞}K°[T^{1/p^∞}]). Let (R_i)_{i∈N} be a projective system of (K°/ϖ^r)[T^{1/p^∞}]-algebras such that for all i ≥ j the canonical maps R_i[j] → R_j[j] ← R_j are almost isomorphisms. Then lim¹_j (R_j)ᵃ = 0.
hypotheses: Only the nested condition R_i[j] ≅ R_j ≅ R_j[j] (almost) is used.
proofSteps: Introduce the triple system R_i[j]_k of submodules spanned by the u^s for s ≤ 1/p^k; as in the limit lemma, lim¹_j (R_j)ᵃ = lim¹_{i,j,k}(R_i[j]_k)ᵃ.
Bound cokernels of transitions: R_i[j+1]_k → R_i[j]_k by ϖ^{1/p^k}, R_i[j]_{k+1} → R_i[j]_k by T^{1/p^k}, and, for i′ ≥ i ≥ j + rp^{k+1}/(p−1), an image comparison giving almost containment.

On a cofinal diagonal j = k, i_k ≥ k + rp^{k+1}/(p−1), the transition cokernels in the almost category are killed by s^{3/p^k}, where s = ϖT. The remaining argument is stronger than termwise almost-zero limit vanishing and is given in the next two steps.

Apply almost elements (·)_*: the cokernel bounds become s^{6/p^k} on the ordinary representative tower N_k, allowing the extra factor needed to lift an almost epimorphism. The comparison (lim¹ N_k)^a ≅ lim¹ (N_k^a) is the module-tower comparison in Gabber–Ramero Lemma 2.4.2(iii), using the Roos product complex. Thus it suffices to show each s^{1/p^l} kills the ordinary Roos cokernel.

Fix ε = 1/p^l and a tail k ≥ N with b_k = 12/p^k ≤ ε. For arbitrary y_k ∈ N_k solve x_k−ψ_k(x_{k+1}) = s^ε y_k by x_k = s^{b_k}z_k: choose z_N = 0 and lift s^{b_k−b_{k+1}}(z_k−s^{ε−b_k}y_k) through ψ_k to obtain z_{k+1}. Such a lift exists because b_k−b_{k+1} ≥ 6/p^k, the cokernel-annihilator exponent. Extend x backwards through the finite head. All powers have exponents in Z[1/p]_{≥0}. Every root of s therefore kills lim¹, proving the almost vanishing.
acceptance: For a constant nested system lim¹ is zero on the nose.

sources.match: Proves almost vanishing of lim¹ for nested systems of root localisations by explicit annihilation estimates on a triple system of submodules.

The almost-elements comparison doubles the transition-cokernel annihilators; a Cauchy product of these ideals makes lim¹ almost zero. The special root-exponent proof is expanded here, rather than attributed to the weaker termwise-zero supplier node.

nodes.title: Compatible systems of perfectoid algebras on the annuli
nodes.statement: Let A be an almost perfectoid K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra with g = T·1 and A[j] := A{ϖ^j/g}, a perfectoid K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/annular-localisation-perfectoid via A[j] ≅ A^♮[j]). The category 2-lim A[j]-Perf has as objects projective systems (B_j)_{j∈N} of perfectoid A[j]-algebras such that, in the canonical factorisation B_i → B_i{ϖ^j/g} → B_j of each transition (i ≥ j), the second map is an isomorphism; morphisms are compatible families of continuous algebra maps. Localisation defines ς : Aˆᵃ-pPerf → 2-lim A[j]-Perf, B ↦ (B[j])_j = (B ⊗̂_A A[j])_j, and the uniform limit defines a functor back.
hypotheses: The systems are strict admissible objects in the sense of Thomason's 2-limits, so 2-lim A[j]-Perf is a categorical 2-limit (André A footnote 22).
proofSteps: B[j] ≅ B ⊗̂_A A[j] by formula (2.24); B[j] is perfectoid since B[j] ≅ B^♮[j] by Gabber's invariance and Proposition 3.6.1.
acceptance: The constant system (A[j])_j is an object; for B′ finite étale over A[1/g], (B′ ⊗ A[j])_j is an object (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.4/annular-envelope).

the finite étale objects of 2-lim A[j]-Perf mediate between almost perfectoid and finite étale A[1/g]-algebras

nodes.title: Uniform limits of nested perfectoid systems are almost perfectoid
nodes.statement: Let A be an almost perfectoid K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra. The localisation functor ς : Aˆᵃ-pPerf → 2-lim A[j]-Perf (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/compatible-annular-system) has the uniform limit ulim as left quasi-inverse and right adjoint. In particular, for every object (B_j) of 2-lim A[j]-Perf the uniform limit ulim B_j is almost perfectoid, and ς is an equivalence of Aˆᵃ-pPerf with a full coreflective subcategory of 2-lim A[j]-Perf.
hypotheses: Essential surjectivity of ς is open in general (André A Question 4.4.3); Proposition 4.4.4 settles it for finite étale systems.
proofSteps: Work in (K°[T^{1/p^∞}], (ϖT)^{1/p^∞}). Apply PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/nested-lim-one-vanishing to R_j = B_j°/ϖ^r, which satisfies R_i[j] ≅ R_j[j] ≅ R_j almost; so lim¹_j(B_j°/ϖ^r)ᵃ = 0.

From the exact sequences 0 → B_j°/ϖ^{1−1/p} → B_j°/ϖ → B_j°/ϖ^{1/p} → 0 and the vanishing of lim¹, the limit sequence stays exact; the ramified criterion of PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/uniform-limit-perfectoid-criterion then makes ulim B_j almost perfectoid (in characteristic p this is immediate since perfectness passes to limits).

ulim∘ς ≅ id by the Riemann extension theorem (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/perfectoid-riemann-extension); the adjunction bijection Hom(ς(C), (B_j)) ≅ Hom(C, ulim B_j) is induced by ulim with inverse given by localisation followed by the canonical map.
acceptance: For the constant system (A[j]) the uniform limit is g^{-1/p^∞}A°[1/ϖ], almost isomorphic to A.
K⟨T⟩-algebras cannot replace K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebras here (André A Remarque 4.4.3(1) with Exemple 3.8.5).

nodes.title: Almost Galois extensions of almost algebras
nodes.statement: Let (V, m) be a basic setup with m ⊗_V m flat (PerfectoidSpaces P0), A → B a monomorphism of commutative almost V-algebras (an extension) and G a finite group acting on B by A-algebra automorphisms. For a set X of A-homomorphisms B → C into a further extension C there is a canonical C-algebra map B ⊗_A C → Π_{χ∈X} C, b ⊗ c ↦ (χ(b)c)_χ; for X = G and C = B this is B ⊗_A B → Π_G B, b ⊗ b′ ↦ (γ(b)b′)_γ. The extension A → B is G-Galois if B^G = A (the invariants being the kernel of B → Π_G B, b ↦ (γb − b)_γ) and B ⊗_A B → Π_G B is an isomorphism; equivalently (B_*)^G = A_* and (B ⊗_A B)_* → Π_G B_* is an isomorphism. Properties (André A Proposition 1.9.1): a G-Galois extension is finite étale of rank |G| with trace the sum of conjugates; G-Galois extensions are stable under base change and descend along faithfully flat maps; for an intermediate extension C with C → B H-Galois for a subgroup H, C ⊗_A B ≅ Π_{G/H} B and C is finite étale of rank [G : H] over A.
hypotheses: Galois for almost algebras does not imply that B_* is Galois over A_*, nor that B_{!!} is Galois over A_{!!} (André A footnote 6): almost elements do not commute with tensor products and (·)_{!!} not with finite products.
proofSteps: Finite projectivity: for η ∈ m choose e_η ∈ B_* ⊗ B_* with e_η² = ηe_η killing the kernel of multiplication and mapping to η; writing e_η = Σ b_i ⊗ b′_i gives Σ γ(b_i)b′_i = 0 for γ ≠ 1 and Σ b_ib′_i = η, so ηb = Σ t(bb_i)b′_i, a factorisation of η·id through a free module (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness). Rank and trace follow by faithfully flat descent from B to A.

Base change: (B ⊗_A A′) ⊗_{A′} (B ⊗_A A′) ≅ (B ⊗_A B) ⊗_A A′ ≅ Π_G B ⊗_A A′, and invariants are computed after faithfully flat base change; the converse is faithfully flat descent (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-faithfully-flat-descent).
Intermediate extensions: after ⊗_C B the canonical map becomes a composite of isomorphisms; descend from B to C.
acceptance: For the trivial group, A → A is Galois; for m = V the notion is the classical Galois extension of rings (Chase–Harrison–Rosenberg).

nodes.title: Galois closures of finite étale extensions and Galois rigidity
nodes.statement: (1) Let R → S be a finite étale extension of rings of constant rank r ≥ 1. There is a Galois extension R → T with group S_r factoring through S such that S → T is Galois with group S_{r−1}: take T the ring of the complement Z of all partial diagonals in the r-fold fibre product Spec S ×_{Spec R} ⋯ ×_{Spec R} Spec S, with S_r permuting the factors. (2) Let G be a finite group of automorphisms of a ring S, R = S^G, and R ⊂ S′ ⊂ S a G-stable intermediate ring that is G-Galois over R. Then S′ = S.
hypotheses: Both statements are classical ring theory. In (1), finite étale extension means faithful, so r ≥ 1; connectedness of Spec R is not required. The construction and proof are supplied by André A §1.9.3, p. 10.
proofSteps: (1) Since S is étale over R the partial diagonals are open and closed, so Z is finite étale over Spec R and over Spec S; S_r × Z → Z ×_X Z (resp. S_{r−1} × Z → Z ×_Y Z) is an isomorphism, checked on geometric fibres where S is a product of r copies of the residue field.
(2) The idempotents e_γ splitting S′ ⊗_R S′ ≅ Π_G S′ also split S ⊗_R S′ ≅ Π_G e_γ(S ⊗_R S′); faithful flatness of S′ over R and taking G × 1 invariants give S ⊗_R S′ = S′ ⊗_R S′, hence S = S′.
acceptance: For r = 1, T = S = R and S_1 is trivial.
For r = 2 and R → S = R[x]/(x² − a) with 2a invertible, T = S.

Rank zero is excluded: over a nonzero ring R, R → 0 cannot factor a faithfully flat Galois extension R → T through 0. For a general finite étale algebra split off its open-and-closed zero-rank locus first.

sources.match: Constructs an S_r-Galois closure of a finite étale extension of constant rank through the complement of partial diagonals, and proves that a G-stable Galois intermediate ring of S over S^G is all of S.

nodes.title: Annular envelopes of finite étale algebras over A[1/g]
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field, ϖ ∈ K°° with |p| ≤ |ϖ| and compatible p-power roots, (V, m) = (K°[T^{1/p^∞}], (ϖT)^{1/p^∞}V) the almost setup, A a perfectoid (or almost perfectoid) K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra, g = T·1 ∈ A° and A[j] = A{ϖ^j/g}. Let B′ be a finite étale A[1/g]-algebra. (1) The algebras B_j = B′ ⊗_{A[1/g]} A[j] form an object of 2-lim A[j]-Perf (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/compatible-annular-system); let B = ulim B_j. (2) The counits B[j] = B{ϖ^j/g} → B_j are isomorphisms. (3) They come from an isomorphism B[1/g] ≅ B′.
hypotheses: A may be replaced by g^{-1/p^∞}A°[1/ϖ] without changing the almost category, so A may be assumed completely integrally closed in A[1/g].
proofSteps: (1) Each B_j is finite étale over the perfectoid A[j], hence perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid); B_i ⊗_{A[i]} A[j] ≅ B_j and, B_i being finite projective over A[i], the tensor product is already complete, equal to B_i{ϖ^j/g}.

(2) The integral closure of A° in B′ maps to the integral closure of A[j]° in B_j, which is B_j° (almost purity: PerfectoidSpaces:P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale); in the limit this gives δ : B′ → B[1/g], and δ_j is a right inverse of η_j. The adjunction of PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/nested-systems-theorem forces δ_jη_j = id.

(3) δ is injective: its kernel I has trace zero in every A[j], hence in A[1/g], which embeds into the algebraic limit lim_j A[j] (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.2/laurent-localisation, injectivity into the limit); I = 0 as B′ is étale. Surjectivity: for B′ Galois with group G, B[1/g]^G = A[1/g] and Galois rigidity (André A Lemme 1.9.3) concludes; in general embed B′ in an S_r-Galois closure (André A Lemme 1.9.2) and take S_{r−1}-invariants.

For the trace argument, first use Laurent limit injectivity to embed A[1/g] in the algebraic projective limit lim_j A[j], where g is invertible. It generally does not embed in the bounded-family uniform limit: 1/T has unbounded annular norms. If I = ker(B′ → lim_j B_j), then tr(xy) maps to zero for x ∈ I and every y ∈ B′, so tr(xy) = 0 by this algebraic-limit embedding. Nondegeneracy of the finite étale trace pairing gives I = 0. On constant-rank components use the Galois closure only for positive rank; the rank-zero algebra is treated separately.
acceptance: For B′ = A[1/g]^n the envelope is the product of n copies of the Riemann extension of A.

sources.match: For a finite étale A[1/g]-algebra B′, shows the base changes to the annuli form a nested perfectoid system whose uniform limit B satisfies B[j] ≅ B_j and B[1/g] ≅ B′, using almost purity, the adjunction of Théorème 4.4.2, a trace argument and a Galois reduction.

nodes.title: Integral almost étaleness of extensions finite étale away from g
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field, ϖ ∈ K°° with |p| ≤ |ϖ| and compatible p-power roots, (V, m) = (K°[T^{1/p^∞}], (ϖT)^{1/p^∞}V) the almost setup, A a perfectoid (or almost perfectoid) K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra, g = T·1 ∈ A° and A[j] = A{ϖ^j/g}. Let B be a perfectoid A-algebra in which g is a nonzerodivisor and such that B[1/g] is finite étale over A[1/g]. Then for every m ≥ 1, B°ᵃ/p^m is a finite étale A°ᵃ/p^m-algebra in the setup (V, m), and B°[1/g] is almost finite étale over A°[1/g] in the setup (K°, K°°). If B[1/g] is Galois over A[1/g] with group G, then B°ᵃ/p^m is Galois over A°ᵃ/p^m with group G in (V, m).
hypotheses: In characteristic p this is Gabber–Ramero 3.5.28 with V = A° and ε = ϖT; the proof below is for characteristic 0.
It is not claimed that B°ᵃ is finite étale over A°ᵃ: the missing ingredient is almost finiteness, because the ideal generated by ϖ is not tight (André A Remarque 5.2.1).
proofSteps: Galois case. Put B_2 = B ⊗_A B and B^{[j]}_2 = B[j] ⊗_{A[j]} B[j]; their completions are perfectoid with (B̂_2)°ᵃ = B°ᵃ ⊗̂ B°ᵃ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula), and B̂_2[j] = B^{[j]}_2.

By the Riemann extension theorem, lim A[j]° = A°_*, lim B[j]° = B°_*, lim B^{[j]°}_2 = g^{-1/p^∞}B̂_2°. Each B[j]°ᵃ is G-Galois over A[j]°ᵃ (André A Proposition 3.4.2, almost purity), so in the limit B°_*^G = A°_* and (B̂_2°)_* ≅ Π_G B°_*.
Reducing modulo p^m gives B°ᵃ/p^m ⊗ B°ᵃ/p^m ≅ Π_G B°ᵃ/p^m, i.e. B°ᵃ/p^m is G-Galois, hence finite étale, over A°ᵃ/p^m (André A Proposition 1.9.1(1)).

After inverting g, almost flatness modulo p and Gabber–Ramero 5.2.1 give almost flatness of B°[1/g] over A°[1/g] in (K°, K°°); separatedness and isometry arguments then place the Galois idempotents in ϖ^{-1/p^∞}B°_2[1/g], so B°[1/g] is almost G-Galois.
General case: reduce to the Galois case as in André A Proposition 3.4.2(2b), using an S_r-Galois closure.
acceptance: If g is a unit this is the almost purity theorem of PerfectoidSpaces P3 modulo p^m.

sources.match: Proves that B°ᵃ/p^m is finite étale (Galois in the Galois case) over A°ᵃ/p^m in the ramified setup and that B°[1/g] is almost finite étale over A°[1/g], via the Riemann extension theorem applied to B ⊗ B.
Explains why almost finite étaleness of B°ᵃ over A°ᵃ is not obtained: almost finiteness is missing and ϖ does not generate a tight ideal.

nodes.title: Ramified almost purity: André's equivalences of categories
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field, ϖ ∈ K°° with |p| ≤ |ϖ| and compatible p-power roots, (V, m) = (K°[T^{1/p^∞}], (ϖT)^{1/p^∞}V) the almost setup, A a perfectoid (or almost perfectoid) K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra, g = T·1 ∈ A° and A[j] = A{ϖ^j/g}. Inverting ϖ and then g induces equivalences between (i) complete A°ᵃ-algebras that are finite étale modulo every power of p and finite étale after inverting g, (ii) almost perfectoid A-algebras that are finite étale after inverting g, and (iii) finite étale A[1/g]-algebras. For g = 1 this recovers the almost purity theorem of PerfectoidSpaces P3.
hypotheses: Whether these categories also agree with finite étale A°ᵃ-algebras is open (André A Question 5.2.2).
proofSteps: Replace A by g^{-1/p^∞}A°[1/ϖ]; by the Riemann extension theorem, A = ulim A[j] and g is a nonzerodivisor.

(ii) → (iii) is an equivalence: in the square formed by localisation ς, forgetting norms and tensoring (B′ ↦ (B′ ⊗ A[j])_j), almost purity makes the bottom functor on finite étale systems an equivalence; σ(B′) = ulim(B′ ⊗ A[j]) is a quasi-inverse by PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.4/annular-envelope and PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/nested-systems-theorem.
(i) → (ii) is fully faithful, and essential surjectivity reduces, since (ii) → (iii) is essentially surjective, to PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.4/integral-ramified-almost-etale.
acceptance: For g = 1 (i) is finite étale A°ᵃ-algebras and the statement is PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence.

nodes.title: The perfectoid Abhyankar envelope of a finite étale A[1/g]-algebra
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field, ϖ ∈ K°° with |p| ≤ |ϖ| and compatible p-power roots, (V, m) = (K°[T^{1/p^∞}], (ϖT)^{1/p^∞}V) the almost setup, A a perfectoid (or almost perfectoid) K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra, g = T·1 ∈ A° and A[j] = A{ϖ^j/g}. For A perfectoid and B′ finite étale over A[1/g], let B̃° be the integral closure of g^{-1/p^∞}A° in B′ and B̃ the integral closure of g^{-1/p^∞}A°[1/ϖ] in B′, with its spectral norm, and let B = ulim_j B′ ⊗_{A[1/g]} A[j]. Then B = B̃; B̃° = (g^{-1/p^∞}A°)^+_{B′} = (ϖg)^{-1/p^∞}B̃° is ϖ-adically complete, and B̃° is almost isomorphic, in (K°[T^{1/p^∞}], T^{1/p^∞}K°°K°[T^{1/p^∞}]), to the integral closure (A°)^+_{B′} of A° in B′. The Abhyankar envelope is B̃^♮, the largest perfectoid A-algebra contained in B′.
hypotheses: Integral closure commutes with localisation, so B̃[1/g] = B′ = B[1/g] (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.4/annular-envelope).
proofSteps: Replace A° by g^{-1/p^∞}A°. The integral closure of A° in B′ maps into each B_j° (André A Lemme 2.4.1(1)), hence into B°; this map of subrings of B′ is injective, and surjective because B° is integral over A° — from the Galois invariants formula (5.6) after reducing to the Galois case.

For the almost comparison, let x satisfy a monic equation with coefficients b_i in g^{-1/p^∞}A°. For any ε = g^{1/p^l}, multiplying the equation by ε^n gives a monic equation for εx with coefficients ε^i b_i ∈ A°. Thus every root of g sends B̃° into (A°)^+_{B′}, while the reverse inclusion is immediate. This proves the asserted almost comparison in the stated ramified setup directly. Maximality of B̃^♮ follows from PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/largest-perfectoid-subalgebra and the coreflection.
acceptance: For B′ = A[1/g], B̃° = g^{-1/p^∞}A° and the envelope is (g^{-1/p^∞}A°[1/ϖ])^♮.

uses.how: the algebra B of the theorem is B̃^♮

nodes.title: André's perfectoid Abhyankar lemma
nodes.statement: Let A be a perfectoid algebra over a perfectoid field K of residue characteristic p, and suppose A contains a compatible system of p-power roots of a nonzerodivisor g ∈ A°; view A° as a K°[T^{1/p^∞}]-algebra via T^{1/p^i} ↦ g^{1/p^i} and work in the setup (K°[T^{1/p^∞}], T^{1/p^∞}K°°[T^{1/p^∞}]). Let B′ be a finite étale A[1/g]-algebra. (1) There is a largest perfectoid A-algebra B contained in B′ such that the structure map A → B is continuous; B[1/g] = B′, and B° is contained in the integral closure of g^{-1/p^∞}A° in B′ and almost isomorphic to it, and also almost isomorphic to the integral closure of A° in B′. (2) For every m ∈ N, B°/p^m is almost finite étale over A°/p^m, and B°[1/g] is almost finite étale over A°[1/g] in the setup (K°, K°°). (3) If B′ is a faithful A[1/g]-module, the trace tr_{B′/A[1/g]} maps B° almost surjectively onto g^{-1/p^∞}A°.
hypotheses: Correction PAPER-ANDRE-18/E13: (1) asserts a continuous structure map A → B whose image lies in B, not an inclusion A ↪ B; an inclusion holds when B′ is faithful over A[1/g], which (3) assumes.
Whether B° is almost finite étale over A° (rather than modulo every p^m) is not established (André A §0.3, Remarque 5.2.1).
proofSteps: Take B = B̃^♮ from PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.4/abhyankar-envelope, which gives (1) and maximality.

(2) Apply PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.4/integral-ramified-almost-etale to the perfectoid algebra B = B̃^♮, with B[1/g] = B′. Transfer the conclusion across the almost isomorphism B°ᵃ ≅ B̃°ᵃ when the integral-closure model is used.

(3) If B′ is faithful then B̃° is a faithful A°-module, and since A → B̃ is isometric, B̃°/p is faithful over A°/p; B̃°ᵃ/p is finite étale over A°ᵃ/p, so the trace is almost surjective modulo p onto (A°ᵃ)_* = g^{-1/p^∞}A°, and almost surjective by the almost Nakayama lemma for complete modules (André A §1.3).
acceptance: For g = 1, (1)–(3) are the almost purity theorem of PerfectoidSpaces P3 (B = B′, B° almost finite étale over A°).

For A = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, g = T and B′ = A[1/T][Y]/(Y^ℓ − T) with ℓ ≠ p prime, B = K⟨T^{1/ℓp^∞}⟩ and B° = K°⟨T^{1/ℓp^∞}⟩ is almost finite étale of rank ℓ over A° in the setup generated by T^{1/p^∞}K°°, although Y^ℓ − T is ramified along T: the monomials T^ε with ε ∈ (1/ℓ)Z[1/p] in a fixed class modulo Z[1/p] have exponents accumulating at 0.
Applied to the perfectoid Kummer tower Â_∞∞ it yields André B Théorème 3.2.1 (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/ramified-kummer-almost-flatness).

nodes.title: Almost perfectoid envelopes of reduced affinoid algebras
nodes.statement: Let K be perfectoid, B a reduced K-affinoid algebra of dimension n, and fix a finite injective Noether-normalisation A = K⟨T_1,…,T_n⟩ → B together with 0 ≠ g ∈ A° such that B[1/g] is finite étale over A[1/g]. Put P = K⟨T_1^{1/p^∞},…,T_n^{1/p^∞},g^{1/p^∞}⟩ and 𝒜 = (g^{-1/p^∞}P°)[1/ϖ], with its spectral norm. Let ℬ be the integral closure of the image of B ⊗_A 𝒜 in B ⊗_A 𝒜[1/g]. Then 𝒜 and ℬ are almost perfectoid, and ℬ°ᵃ/p^m is finite étale over 𝒜°ᵃ/p^m for every m, in the setup (K°[T^{1/p^∞}], (ϖT)^{1/p^∞}K°[T^{1/p^∞}]) with T^{1/p^h} ↦ g^{1/p^h}.
hypotheses: The construction depends on the choice of Noether normalisation and discriminant g.

Noether normalisation supplies a finite injection. The additional choice making B[1/g] étale is part of this presentation; it is not a conclusion of the cited normalisation node alone. The zero affinoid is handled separately.
proofSteps: Use AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-noether-normalisation for the finite injection; retain the explicit hypothesis on g. The root algebra P is perfectoid. RA.3 root saturation and Riemann extension make 𝒜 almost perfectoid. Apply the annular-envelope and Abhyankar-envelope construction to B ⊗_A 𝒜[1/g]; apply integral almost étaleness to its perfectoid coreflection and transfer along the almost isomorphism of unit balls. This gives the assertion for ℬ without treating an almost perfectoid algebra as a perfectoid one.
acceptance: For B = A one gets 𝒜 itself.
The construction does not require toric coordinates, in contrast with the usual logarithmic almost purity constructions (André A §0.5).

nodes.title: Pure (universally injective) module and ring maps
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring. An R-linear map u : M → N is pure if P ⊗_R u : P ⊗_R M → P ⊗_R N is injective for every R-module P; it suffices to test finitely presented P. A ring map R → S is pure if R → S is pure as a map of R-modules, equivalently R′ → S ⊗_R R′ is injective for every R-algebra R′ (universally injective). Properties (André B Annexe A, after Lazard): M ⊂ N is pure iff Hom(P, N) → Hom(P, N/M) is surjective for all finitely presented P; if N/M is finitely presented, M ⊂ N is pure iff M is a direct summand; pure maps are the filtered colimits of split injections; pure maps are Tor-injective; if N is flat, M ⊂ N is pure iff N/M is flat; pure maps of S-modules are pure over R. Pure ring maps are stable under composition, products, base change and filtered colimits; if R → S → T is pure so is R → S; if R → S → T is flat and S → T pure then R → S is flat; R → S is pure iff base change Mod_R → Mod_S is faithful; faithfully flat iff pure and flat; if S is finitely presented as an R-module, R → S is pure iff it has an R-linear retraction iff S is a generator.
hypotheses: In the generator criterion the dual is Hom_R(S, R) (misprint PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/E1).
proofSteps: Lazard's characterisation via finitely presented modules and filtered colimits of split monomorphisms; Tor-injectivity follows since filtered colimits commute with Tor.
Ring-level statements follow from the module-level ones by taking symmetric algebras and the faithfulness criterion as in André B Lemme A.2.1.

For the generator criterion use the trace ideal generated by f(s), with f ∈ Hom_R(S,R). If it is R, choose finitely many pairs (f_i,s_i) with Σ_i f_i(s_i) = 1. Then t ↦ Σ_i f_i(s_i t) is an R-linear retraction S → R. The generator property does not require a single evaluation f(s) to equal 1.
acceptance: Every split injection is pure; a faithfully flat ring map is pure.

nodes.title: Almost pure maps
nodes.statement: Let (V, m) be a basic setup with m ⊗_V m flat (PerfectoidSpaces P0), R a V-algebra and u : M → N a map of R-modules. Then u is almost pure if P ⊗_R u is almost injective (its kernel is killed by m) for every R-module P (equivalently every finitely presented P); equivalently M^a_! → N^a_! is pure. A map of V-algebras R → S is almost pure if it is almost pure as a map of R-modules, equivalently R^a_{!!} → S^a_{!!} is pure. If M ⊂ N is almost pure, then Hom_R(P, N) → Hom_R(P, N/M) is almost surjective for every finitely presented P; in particular, if N/M is finitely presented, M is an almost direct summand of N and the class of N in Ext^1_R(N/M, M) is almost zero. If R → S → T is almost pure then so is R → S, and if M → M′ → N with M → N almost pure then M → M′ is almost pure. An almost faithfully flat map of almost algebras is almost pure.
hypotheses: Corrections PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/E10–E11: purity of M → N is tested on P ⊗ M → P ⊗ N, and the intermediate factorisation is M → M′ → N.

The published A.4, p. 92, already tensors M → N correctly. The malformed ring-map expression in the module definition occurs only in arXiv:1609.00345v1 §5.5, p. 14; this is a version-specific source issue, not an error in the published definition.
proofSteps: The left adjoint (·)_! is exact and commutes with ⊗ (Gabber–Ramero 2.2.24, 2.4.35), so almost injectivity of P ⊗ u is injectivity of its (·)_!; this gives the equivalence with purity of M^a_! → N^a_!.
Lemme A.4.1 follows from Lazard's lifting criterion applied to N^a_! (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/pure-map): taking P = N/M gives, for each η ∈ m, f : N/M → N projecting to η·id.
For algebras, (·)_{!!} commutes with ⊗ and φ is almost injective iff φ^a_{!!} is injective (Gabber–Ramero 3.1.3(ii), 3.4.2).
Almost faithfully flat ⇒ almost pure: (·)_{!!} preserves faithful flatness (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness), and faithfully flat maps are pure.
acceptance: For m = V (trivial setup) almost purity is purity.

nodes.title: Krull detection along faithfully flat algebras with an idempotent ideal
nodes.statement: Let R be a Noetherian ring, M a finitely generated R-module, S a faithfully flat R-algebra and K an idempotent ideal of S with K·(M ⊗_R S) = 0. Then for every s ∈ R whose image lies in K there is r ∈ Ann_R(M) with (1 − r)s = 0. In particular, if R is local and the preimage of K in R is nonzero, then M = 0.
hypotheses: This is the published statement; arXiv v1 has a different version with an ideal J and K ⊂ JS (both versions are proved the same way).
proofSteps: Let J = Ann_R M. By flatness J S = Ann_S(M ⊗ S), so K ⊂ JS and K = K^n ⊂ J^nS for all n.
By purity of R → S (faithful flatness), R ∩ J^nS = J^n, so the preimage of K lies in ⋂_n J^n.
Krull's intersection theorem (Mathlib Ideal.mem_iInf_smul_pow_eq_bot_iff) gives r ∈ J with (1 − r)s = 0; in the local case 1 − r is a unit unless J is the unit ideal, and then M = 0.
acceptance: If K = 0 the statement is empty.
Noetherianity of R is necessary: for R = S = K° (K perfectoid), M = K°/K°° and K = K°° (idempotent), K kills M ⊗ S and R ∩ K ≠ 0, yet M ≠ 0.

nodes.title: The normalized two-index Kummer tower over W(k)⟦T_1,…,T_n⟧
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W(k) its Witt vectors, K_0 = W(k)[1/p], K_j = K_0(ζ_{p^j}) with ζ_{p^j} a compatible system of primitive p^j-th roots of unity, K_∞ = ⋃ K_j and K̂_∞ its p-adic completion, a perfectoid field. Let A = W(k)⟦T_1,…,T_n⟧ and 0 ≠ g ∈ A. For (j, k) ∈ N², put K_j°⟦T^{1/p^j}_{≤n}⟧[g^{1/p^k}] = K_j°⟦T_1^{1/p^j},…,T_n^{1/p^j}⟧[X]/(X^{p^k} − g) and A_jk = K_j°⟦T^{1/p^j}_{≤n}⟧[g^{1/p^k}][1/p], a double inductive system of K_0-algebras with the natural inclusions; infinite indices mean directed unions. Let A°_jk be the integral closure of A in A_jk. Then A°_jk contains K_j°⟦T^{1/p^j}⟧[g^{1/p^k}] and A_jk = A°_jk[1/p]; for (j, k) ∈ N² it is Noetherian and p-adically complete; A°_{j0} = K_j°⟦T^{1/p^j}⟧ and A°_{00} = A; A°_{j′k′} = A°_jk ∩ A_{j′k′} for j′ ≤ j, k′ ≤ k; for j = ∞, A°_{∞k} is the increasing union of Noetherian rings finite over one another, each integrally closed relative to its specified generic algebra; A°_{∞k} is completely integrally closed relative to A_{∞k}. These generic algebras and models may have zero divisors. The maps A°_{j0} → A°_{j′0} are finite and faithfully flat (indeed free), A°_{∞0} is faithfully flat over each A°_{j0}, and so is its p-adic completion Â°_{∞0}, which is isomorphic to W(k⟦T^{1/p^∞}_{≤n}⟧) ⊗̂_{W(k)} K̂_∞°.

Its total quotient algebra is a finite product of finite field extensions of Frac(A), all separable in characteristic zero. Mathlib IsIntegralClosure.finite gives a finite A-module D by normalizing A in each field factor (A is normal and Noetherian). Then A°_jk = D ∩ A_jk is an A-submodule of D, hence finite, Noetherian and p-adically complete. This is integral closedness relative to A_jk, without asserting that A°_jk is a normal domain or equals D. The intersection formula follows from integrality over A and injectivity of the tower maps.

A°_{j0} = K_j°⟦T^{1/p^j}⟧ because this ring is regular, hence normal, and integral over A; the transitions are free of finite rank with basis monomials, hence faithfully flat; completion preserves faithful flatness over the Noetherian A°_{j0} (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1/faithful-flat-algebra-completion).

For relative complete integral closedness in R = A°_{∞k} ⊂ S = A_{∞k} = R[1/p], use exactly the pinned definition IsAlmostIntegral: let x ∈ S and let d be a nonzerodivisor of R with d x^m ∈ R for every m. Choose a finite generic stage A_jl containing both x and d. Each d x^m is integral over A, and the intersection formula puts it in A°_jl. Multiplication by d embeds the A-module A[x] into the finite A-module A°_jl: d remains a nonzerodivisor after inverting p, hence on this stage. Noetherianity of A makes A[x] finite, so x is integral over A and belongs to R. This also treats k = ∞. For arbitrary perfect k, ζ_{p^j} = ζ_{p^{j+1}}^p and perfectness of k give surjectivity of Frobenius from K_{j+1}°/p onto K_j°/p. The valuations of ζ_{p^j}−1 tend to zero. nodes.title: The spectral norm of the Kummer tower and isometric transitions
nodes.statement: In the setting of PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/normalized-kummer-tower, there is a unique K_∞-algebra norm on A_{∞k} with unit ball A°_{∞k}, and it is spectral. With the induced norms, the unit ball of A_jk is A°_jk and all transition maps of the system (A°_jk) are isometric. The algebras A_{j0} are multiplicatively normed (this can fail for k ≠ 0), and the ideal A°°_{∞0} of topologically nilpotent elements of A°_{∞0} is an idempotent prime ideal equal to K°°_∞A°_{∞0}.
hypotheses: Density of |K_∞| in R_{>0} is used for uniqueness and spectrality.
proofSteps: A°_{∞k} is completely integrally closed (normalized-kummer-tower), so by the unit-ball dictionary (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.2/unit-ball-dictionary (c)–(d)) its gauge norm is the unique spectral norm with this unit ball; isometry of transitions follows from A°_{j′k′} = A°_jk ∩ A_{j′k′} and the isometry criterion (a).

For k = 0 the norm on A_{j0} is the Gauss-type sup norm of coefficients, multiplicative because the reduction k⟦T^{1/p^j}⟧ is a domain; A°°_{∞0} = K°°_∞A°_{∞0} is prime because A°_{∞0}/K°°_∞ = k⟦T^{1/p^∞}⟧ is a domain (André A 2.2.1–2.2.2).

nodes.title: The completed Kummer tower as a colimit of tubes; perfectoidness
nodes.statement: In the setting of PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/normalized-kummer-tower, let Â_∞0⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ be the completion of A_∞0[T^{1/p^∞}] for the multiplicative Gauss norm (equivalently, complete the integral Gauss unit ball p-adically and then invert p), so that Â_∞0⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩° = Â°_∞0⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = Â_∞0⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩_{≤1} and T − g has norm 1. In the almost setup (K°_∞, K°°_∞) there is a canonical isomorphism Â°ᵃ_∞∞ ≅ completed colim_i (Â_∞0⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩{(T − g)/ϖ^i}°)ᵃ, the completion being p-adic. The K̂_∞-algebra Â_∞0 is perfectoid, hence so are Â_∞0⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and Â_∞∞ = Â_∞0⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩.

Algebraic (p)-adic completion after p is inverted would be the zero ring and is not the construction intended here. The root algebra freely adjoins a compatible root system, even when g = 1; it is not obtained by choosing the root 1 at every stage.

Â_∞∞ is the root algebra Â_∞0⟨g^{1/p^∞}⟩ (the A_jk adjoin compatible roots of g, and the spectral norms agree by isometry), so it is perfectoid by PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/perfectoid-root-algebra; the colimit formula is the unit-ball form of the tubular-colimit theorem (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.2/tubular-colimit) for A = Â_∞0.

nodes.title: Faithful flatness of the Noetherian tube models
nodes.statement: In the setting of PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/normalized-kummer-tower, let j ≥ k be finite, ϖ_j a uniformizer of K_j°, 0 ≠ ϖ_{ik} ∈ K_j with |ϖ_{ik}| < |ϖ_j|, f_{ik} ∈ A°_{j0}⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩ and g_k ∈ A°_{j0} with f_{ik} ≡ T^{1/p^k} − g_k modulo ϖ_j. Then C = A°_{j0}⟨T^{1/p^j}, U⟩/(ϖ_{ik}U − f_{ik}) = A_{j0}⟨T^{1/p^j}⟩{f_{ik}/ϖ_{ik}}_{≤1} is a Noetherian, ϖ_j-torsion-free, ϖ_j-adically complete A°_{j0}-algebra with C/ϖ_j ≅ (A°_{j0}/ϖ_j)[T^{1/p^j}, U]/(T^{1/p^k} − g_k) free over A°_{j0}/ϖ_j; hence C is faithfully flat over A°_{j0}.
